title: Audit telemetry: hotpath eviction & adaptive retention policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Audit telemetry volume has grown 3x YOY. Current retention policy keeps fully indexed events in hot store for 90 days, causing sustained shard inflation and per-tenant cost spikes. We lack an automated, policy-driven mechanism to demote low-value events to compacted/cold storage or evict duplicate/noisy events while preserving compliance traces for security and SSO/SAML investigations.

Goal: Implement a predictable, cost-aware retention and hotpath eviction system that: 1) applies RBAC v2 labels to govern access and retention tiers; 2) demotes traffic to compacted coldstore according to TTLs, tags, and query SLAs; 3) performs streaming compaction to reduce index size for long-tail events; 4) exposes admin controls (console + API) to override retention for legal/incident holds; 5) integrates with existing SSO/SAML attribute mapping so audit events that relate to admin actions are retained in hotstore longer.

Scope: Ingestion transform, partitioning rules, compaction strategy, admin override API, dashboards, and rollout for hosted + Dedicated (reserved) deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline tags each event with rbv:role and tenant retention class derived from RBAC v2 labels and SAML attributes
Events can be demoted from hot to compacted coldstore after policy evaluation without data loss for compliance queries
Storage cost per 100k events reduced by >=30% in 60 days within test tenant
Admin console exposes per-tenant retention override and holds; actions are audited
Automated tests cover eviction policy, demotion correctness, and access controls via RBAC v2
design_notes: Ingest: insert a lightweight policy-evaluator stage in the streaming pipeline that enriches events with retention_tier, rbv_role, and hold_id. This runs after normalization and before indexing.

Partitioning: use time + retention_tier + tenant_id as partition key. Hot partitions = 7-day rolling shards optimized for reads; Warm partitions = 30-day compacted segments; Coldstore = blob objects with compacted index summaries for >30 days.

Compaction: streaming compaction worker performs per-tenant, per-event-type dedupe and delta-compression; produce compacted index (min, max timestamp, fingerprint map) to satisfy tail compliance queries without full index scan.
Indexing trade-off: full-text indexing of admin-sensitive events (RBAC root/admin actions) for 90 days; probabilistic/minimal indexing for high-volumes (metrics, heartbeats) to save index space.

Admin controls: Console UI + API for legal hold or emergency retention override; overrides create a hold_id attached to events and prevent demotion until released. Actions are recorded in audit_store with SSO user and session id.

Security: SAML attributes (group, role, entitlements) mapped during authentication flow are included in event envelope to enforce retention policies tied to RBAC v2. Ensure PII minimization and KMS encryption at rest for sensitive fields.
Observability: add retention_tier and demotion_reason tags to telemetry; expose real-time shard utilization and projected 30-day cost delta per tenant in Console
Rollout plan: start with opt-in 'cost-aware' toggle for internal infra tenants, then Selected Beta for 5 customers, then full rollout after 6 weeks of monitoring
milestones: Compaction worker MVP deployed to staging - 2025-03-18
Beta rollout to tenants & cost validation - 2025-03-25
risks: Over-aggressive demotion may break customer investigations — mitigated by conservative default TTLs and admin holds
Index compaction bugs could make some fields expensive to reconstruct — maintain raw blob with compacted index for 180 days as fallback
Per-tenant variance: high-cardinality tenants may still drive costs; add tenant-level hard limits and quota alerts
Security: retention override must be RBAC-gated and logged to prevent misuse
